title: Families on the decks of Divis Flats, 1980
episode: 1980: Living in the Dilapidated DIVIS FLATS | Nationwide | Voice of the People | BBC Archive
description: A 1980 report from the BBC’s Nationwide magazine show hears from tenants of Divis Flats, the damp, overcrowded 1960s deck-access estate in west Belfast. All but Divis Tower was demolished in the 1990s.

title: A night at the most bombed hotel, 1973
episode: 1973: A NIGHT at the EUROPA - the World's MOST BOMBED HOTEL | Nationwide | 1970s | BBC Archive
description: BBC Nationwide spends a night in 1973 at the Europa Hotel on Great Victoria Street, opened in 1971 and bombed again and again during the Troubles, the 30-year conflict over Northern Ireland. It was home to the visiting press corps.

title: The narrow lanes of the old town
description: Local history channel Document Belfast walks the entries, the narrow alleys running off High Street in the old town, such as Pottinger’s Entry and Winecellar Entry, home to some of the city’s oldest pubs.

title: Snugs, tiles and gaslight in a Victorian pub
episode: History and HIDDEN SECRETS of the Crown Bar Belfast - One of Belfast's Most Historic Pubs
place: Crown Liquor Saloon, Great Victoria Street
description: Document Belfast looks round the Crown Liquor Saloon, a Victorian gin palace on Great Victoria Street with stained glass, mosaic tiles and carved wooden snugs, owned by the National Trust and still a working pub.

title: The house of endless books where Narnia began
episode: Surprised by Joy at "Little Lea", C.S. Lewis's Childhood Home in Belfast
description: Lewis scholar Jason Lepojärvi reads from C. S. Lewis’s memoir Surprised by Joy at Little Lea, the east Belfast house the family moved into in 1905, whose rooms of books and attic games fed the boy who later wrote Narnia.

title: Inside the white parliament on the hill
description: The Northern Ireland Assembly’s own tour of Parliament Buildings at Stormont, the Portland stone parliament opened in 1932 at the top of a mile-long avenue in east Belfast, now home to the devolved Northern Ireland Assembly.
